openwrt_wiki.Einleitung: The Cudy TR3000 is a router designed for travel and portable use. It's powered with USB-C and features a USB3 port, Wi-Fi 6, and 1x2.5G WAN + 1x1G LAN port
openwrt_wiki.Hardware Highlights: The router has 3 WiFi antennas (two non-detachable external, and one internal). The internal antenna is for zero-wait DFS functionality only.
OEM easy installation: Determine the size of the flash on your device: 128 MB or 256 MB. You can find it on the carton or the label on your device (exact wording varies by market).

Download the Intermediate Firmware: https://www.cudy.com/blogs/faq/openwrt-software-download (Google Drive). The file is "TR3000 V1.zip" (or "TR3000 V1_20251118.zip" for the updated version (to support the newer flash?)). Note that the 256 MB version has a separate firmware in the "TR3000 256 MB Flash V1 (Not for TR3000 V1)" folder. Wrong firmware will be rejected and will not brick your device.
Extract the file "cudy_tr3000-v1-sysupgrade.bin" from the zip file.

Enter the web interface at http://192.168.10.1/ with the default password "admin" (or the password you set during the initial setup of newer stock firmware). Go to "Upgrade Firmware" ... Wait 2 minutes.
Intermediate firmware: connect via Ethernet (OpenWrt doesn't enable Wi-Fi at first install), LuCI at http://192.168.1.1/, then flash sysupgrade from firmware-selector.openwrt.org
openwrt_wiki.OEM installation using TFTP and U-Boot c: Warning: Cudy TR3000 request special tools for uart jumper. UART (GND, TX, RX); router off, hold RESET, power on, keep >=5 s; TFTP OEM recovery fails after 5 s, then U-Boot shell; PC 192.168.1.88/24; setenv bootfile initramfs-kernel.bin; tftpboot; bootm; then sysupgrade
openwrt_wiki.Switching to OpenWrt U-Boot layout: The default available router space is around 45 MB in the 128 MB version. Replacing the stock bootloader with the OpenWrt U-Boot bootloader increases available storage space from 45 MB to 93 MB. Warning: may cause a soft brick. Ablauf: nanddump-Sicherung aller mtd, kmod-mtd-rw i_want_a_brick=1, BL2 = cudy_tr3000-v1-ubootmod-preloader.bin, FIP = ubootmod-bl31-uboot.fip, TFTP-Recovery mit PC 192.168.1.254 und ubootmod-initramfs-recovery.itb, ubiformat mtd5, ubootenv-Volumes, sysupgrade ubootmod-squashfs-sysupgrade.itb
openwrt_wiki.Debricking: Cudy bootloader starts a TFTP client for OEM recovery using the Reset button, but this only accepts OEM firmware. Hard bricks (as long as preloader output can be seen over serial) can be recovered using mtk_uartboot with mt7981-ram-ddr3-bl2.bin and cudy_tr3000-v1-ubootmod-bl31-uboot.fip
openwrt_wiki.Flash Layout: SLC SPI-NAND flash memory chip, spi0.0 128 MiB: BL2 1 MiB | u-boot-env 512 KiB | factory 2 MiB | bdinfo 256 KiB | FIP 2 MiB | ubi 64 MiB (kernel, rootfs SquashFS, rootfs_data UBIFS)
openwrt_wiki.Opening the case: Remove the 4 rubber pads underneath (heat slightly), remove 4 screws (small Philips), bottom clipped to top with small tabs
openwrt_wiki.Serial / UART: On the bottom of the PCB you can find two small test points. If your PCB has the ethernet ports at left and the LEDs at right, then the left test point is RX and the right is TX. GND: any GND point on the board. Solder wires or use needles. 115200, 8N1, 3.3V

installation.wert: zweistufig: Cudy-signierte Zwischenfirmware, dann Gluon-sysupgrade (Weg A, nicht automatisierbar)
